Bug_Title: "@Bean" methods for Singleton should not be invoked in "@Configuration" when proxyBeanMethods is false
Bug_Details:
When setting the proxyBeanMethods attribute to false the @Bean methods are not proxied and this is similar
to removing the @Configuration stereotype. In this scenario, @Bean methods within the @Configuration annotated
class operate in lite
mode , resulting in a new bean creation each time the method is invoked.
For Singleton beans, this could cause unexpected outcomes as the bean is created multiple times instead of being created once and
cached.
The rule raises an issue when the proxyBeanMethods attribute is set to false and the @Bean method of a Singleton bean is directly invoked in the @Configuration annotated class code.
Bug_Explanation: In the `BugExample` class, the `getSingletonBean` method directly invokes the `singletonBean` method which acts as a @Bean method for Singleton bean. However, since the `proxyBeanMethods` attribute is set to false in the `@Configuration` annotation, this results in a new instance of the SingletonBean being created every time `getSingletonBean` is called, rather than caching the bean and returning the same instance.

Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered by calling the `showBug` method from the `BugExample` class. The `showBug` method creates two instances of the `SingletonBean` and checks if they are the same. Since the `proxyBeanMethods` attribute is set to false in the `BugExample` class, a new `SingletonBean` is created each time the `getSingletonBean` method is invoked. Therefore, the test case should fail at the assertion `assertFalse(bugExample.showBug())`.
